title: Logs, lessons, exception and end project reports
blurb: Explain the purpose of the daily log, lessons log, lessons report, exception report, end project report and the digital and data management approach in an agile project.
question: A project manager wants somewhere to note an informal issue, a required action and a significant event from today's meeting. Which product should be used?

teach.h: The rest of the progress toolkit
teach.body: Besides the dashboards, the progress practice in PRINCE2 Agile keeps several familiar PRINCE2 products: the daily log, the lessons log, the lessons report, the exception report and the end project report, plus the digital and data management approach. That approach describes how data and information will be created, used and managed across the project ecosystem, through the lifecycle and afterwards, including security and privacy. Agile changes how these are used, not why they exist.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 12.3.2, Table 12.1; PRINCE2 7 digital and data management approach

teach.body: The daily log records informal issues, required actions and significant events. The project manager creates it very early, in starting up a project, during 'appoint the project executive and project manager'. The lessons log is a repository for lessons that apply to this project or to future ones; in 'assess previous lessons' the project manager reviews lessons from similar projects and, if appropriate, creates it. Both form part of the project log.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, Table 13.1

teach.body: Agile teams learn constantly, especially in retrospectives. The lessons report exists to share lessons and trigger actions so that they become embedded in the organization's ways of working, not just written down. In closing a project the project manager reviews the project log for lessons that future projects could use and puts them in the lessons report; the closure workshop can add insights and trends from Agilometer and psychological safety assessments.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, Table 13.18, Table 13.19

teach.h: Exception report and end project report
teach.body: The exception report informs the board when a stage plan or project plan is forecast to exceed its tolerances, offering options and a recommendation; in agile the project manager first assesses options against the release map and project canvas. The end project report reviews how the project performed against the version of the PID used to authorize it. It is prepared in 'evaluate the project' when closing a project.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, Table 13.9, Table 13.18

head: Question
What it covers
rows: How data and information are created, used, managed

teach.body: Project manager Kofi Mensah is appointed to Saltmarsh's online booking project and opens a daily log the same week, noting an informal concern about payment provider contracts. He reviews lessons from last year's timetable app and starts a lessons log. Team retrospectives keep adding to it. When a stage forecast shows the Musts will not fit, he sends an exception report. At closure he prepares the end project report against the original PID and a lessons report that leads to a new testing standard.

teach.text: The lessons LOG stores lessons; the lessons REPORT shares them and triggers action to embed them. The daily log is created in STARTING UP, not initiation. And the END PROJECT report (performance against the PID used to authorize the project) is not the end stage report, which the project dashboard replaces.

items: Daily log: informal issues, required actions, significant events; created by the PM in starting up.
Lessons log: repository of lessons for this or future projects.
Lessons report: shares lessons and triggers actions to embed them in ways of working.
Exception report: stage or project plan forecast to exceed tolerance, with options and recommendation.
End project report: performance against the PID version used to authorize the project.
Digital and data management approach: how data and information are created, used and managed, with security and privacy.

summary: You can now explain the purpose of the daily log, lessons log, lessons report, exception report and end project report in an agile project. You can also say what the digital and data management approach covers.

A.q: What is the daily log used for?
options: Recording lessons that apply to this or future projects
Recording informal issues, required actions and significant events
Recording the status of every product in the plan
Recording formal issues, change requests and off-specifications
A.why: Table 12.1: the daily log records informal issues, required actions or significant events.

whyNot.0: Lessons for this or future projects go in the lessons log.
whyNot.2: Product status is held in the product register.
whyNot.3: Formal issues are recorded in the issue register.

A.q: What is the purpose of the end project report?
options: To review how the project performed against the PID used to authorize it
To show the board regular status for the stage in progress
To tell the board that stage tolerances are forecast to be exceeded
To list every user story delivered across the final release
A.why: Table 12.1: the end project report reviews how the project performed against the version of the PID used to authorize it.

whyNot.1: Regular stage status is the highlight report, replaced by the project dashboard.
whyNot.2: A forecast breach of tolerance is reported in an exception report.
whyNot.3: Delivered stories are visible in the backlogs and burn charts; the report judges overall performance.

A.q: Which product shares lessons and triggers actions so that they become embedded in the organization's ways of working?
options: Lessons log
Daily log
Team dashboard
Lessons report
A.why: Table 12.1: the lessons report shares lessons and triggers actions to embed them in ways of working.

whyNot.0: The lessons log stores lessons; it does not by itself trigger organizational action.
whyNot.1: The daily log records informal issues, actions and events.
whyNot.2: The team dashboard shows team progress and replaces the checkpoint report.

B.q: In which process and activity does the project manager create the daily log?
options: Initiating a project, agree the management approaches
Starting up a project, appoint the executive and PM
Controlling a stage, capture issues and risks
Directing a project, authorize initiation
B.why: Table 13.1: in 'appoint the project executive and project manager' (starting up a project) the project manager creates the daily log.

whyNot.0: The daily log already exists by initiation; it is created in starting up.
whyNot.2: Issues and risks are captured during the stage, long after the daily log is created.
whyNot.3: Authorize initiation is a board decision; the PM creates the daily log in starting up.

B.q: What does the digital and data management approach describe?
options: How data and information are created, used and managed
How progress is shown to the board on dashboards
How the team stores code and test scripts each iteration
How lessons are shared with other projects
B.why: It describes how data and information will be created, used and managed across the project ecosystem, through the lifecycle and afterwards, including security and privacy.

whyNot.1: Dashboards show progress; the approach covers data handling more broadly.
whyNot.2: Team tooling may follow the approach, but the approach covers all project data, not one team's code.
whyNot.3: Sharing lessons is the job of the lessons report.

B.q:
Which two statements about logs and reports in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. The lessons log is a repository of lessons for this or future projects.
2. The exception report replaces the highlight report.
3. The exception report offers options and a recommendation to the board.
4. The daily log is created in the project initiation workshop.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 4
2 and 3
2 and 4
B.why: The lessons log stores lessons for this or future projects (1), and the exception report offers options and a recommendation (3) (Table 12.1).

whyNot.1: Statement 4 is wrong: the daily log is created in starting up a project.
whyNot.2: Statement 2 is wrong: the project dashboard replaces the highlight report.
whyNot.3: Both are wrong: the project dashboard replaces the highlight report, and the daily log comes from starting up.

C.q: During closing a project, what does the project manager do in 'evaluate the project'?
options: Prepares an exception plan and updates the release map
Updates the team dashboards and the Agilometer
Prepares the end project report and the lessons report
Confirms benefits and closes the daily log
C.why: Table 13.18: the PM reviews the PID's original intent and approved changes, prepares an end project report, and reviews the project log for lessons to include in the lessons report.

whyNot.0: Exception plans are prepared at a stage boundary, not when evaluating the project.
whyNot.1: Team dashboards are kept by teams; evaluating the project is about the end project and lessons reports.
whyNot.3: Confirming benefits is not what evaluating the project does; it centres on the end project and lessons reports.

C.q: A team retrospective finds that pairing testers with developers halved rework. The organization wants future projects to adopt this. Which product is BEST used, and why?
options: The daily log, because it records significant events
The lessons report, because it triggers action to embed lessons
The exception report, because it goes to the board
The team dashboard, because it is reviewed in retrospectives
C.why: The lessons report shares lessons and triggers actions so they become embedded in the organization's ways of working (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The daily log is the PM's informal record; it does not spread lessons to other projects.
whyNot.2: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of tolerance, not lessons.
whyNot.3: The team dashboard shows team progress; it does not embed lessons across the organization.

C.q: A stage plan is forecast to exceed tolerance. Which product informs the board, and what must it include?
options: The project dashboard, with burn charts and risks
The issue report, with one issue's impact analysis
The lessons report, with improvement actions for teams
The exception report, with options and a recommendation
C.why: Table 12.1: the exception report informs the board when a stage or project plan is forecast to exceed tolerance and offers options and a recommendation.

whyNot.0: The project dashboard gives regular status; a forecast breach needs an exception report.
whyNot.1: An issue report covers one issue's impact; a forecast tolerance breach needs an exception report.
whyNot.2: A lessons report shares lessons; it does not escalate a breach.

reteach.title: A ship's paperwork
reteach.question: What would a ship's captain keep, and what would they send home?

blocks.body: A captain keeps a daily logbook of small events and actions (daily log) and a notebook of lessons about the route (lessons log). If the ship will clearly miss port on time, a telegram goes to the owners with options (exception report). At voyage end, a final account compares the voyage with the plan the owners approved (end project report), and a note goes to the shipping line so every ship adopts what worked (lessons report).

blocks.text: A notebook of lessons (log) changes nothing until a note goes out and is acted on (report).

explain.body: Informal issues, required actions and significant events. Created by the PM in starting up, in 'appoint the project executive and project manager' (Table 12.1, Table 13.1).

test.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The [?] log records informal issues, required actions and significant events.
options: lessons
daily
issue
quality
test.why: The daily log records informal issues, required actions or significant events (Table 12.1).

whyNot.2: Formal issues go in the issue register.
whyNot.3: The quality register records quality activities and their results.

explain.body: The log is the store of lessons; the report shares them and triggers action to embed them in ways of working (Table 12.1).

test.q: What is the main difference between the lessons log and the lessons report?
options: The log is for the board; the report is for the delivery teams
The log covers project risks; the report covers project issues
The log stores lessons; the report shares them and triggers action
The log is written at closure; the report is updated daily
test.why: The lessons log is a repository; the lessons report shares lessons and triggers actions to embed them (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The difference is storing versus sharing and embedding, not the audience.
whyNot.1: Risks and issues have their own registers.
whyNot.3: The lessons log is kept throughout; lessons reports can be produced at stage ends and closure.

explain.body: Reviews how the project performed against the version of the PID used to authorize it; prepared in 'evaluate the project' (Table 12.1, Table 13.18).

test.q: Against what does the end project report review the project's performance?
options: The latest release map
The project canvas agreed during starting up a project
The team dashboards from the final delivery stage
The version of the PID used to authorize the project
test.why: Table 12.1: the end project report reviews performance against the version of the PID used to authorize the project.

whyNot.0: The release map shows plans; the benchmark is the PID used to authorize the project.
whyNot.1: The project canvas from starting up comes before the PID was approved.
whyNot.2: Team dashboards show team progress, not the benchmark for the project.

explain.body: How data and information are created, used and managed across the project ecosystem, through the lifecycle and afterwards, including security and privacy. Defined in 'agree the management approaches' (Table 13.6).

test.q: In which activity is the digital and data management approach defined?
options: Agree the management approaches, initiating a project
Assess previous lessons, starting up a project
Report highlights, controlling a stage
Evaluate the project, closing a project
test.why: Table 13.6: in 'agree the management approaches' the PM, with the team, defines approaches including digital and data.

whyNot.1: Assess previous lessons reviews lessons and may create the lessons log.
whyNot.2: Report highlights updates the project dashboard.
whyNot.3: Evaluate the project prepares the end project report.
